title: What happened in LTO tape in October 2026
answer: LTO tape storage news for October 2026: 40 TB LTO-10 cartridges sold for about $494, well below their list price, Spectra Logic added an Italian distributor, cheap used LTO-5 drives drew homelab interest, TapeArk began moving old tape archives into cloud virtual tape libraries, and still no half-height LTO-10 drive is on sale.

items.headline: 40 TB LTO-10 cartridges sell for about $494
items.summary: Chinese tech site IT Home reported Fujifilm's 40 TB native LTO-10 cartridge selling for about $494, far below the $888.89 suggested retail price. Our September price check found 40 TB cartridges at $491 to $555 at US sellers.

items.headline: Spectra Logic signs Italian distributor ICOS
items.summary: Tape library maker Spectra Logic signed a distribution agreement with ICOS S.p.A., giving ICOS's Italian channel partners access to Spectra's storage products.

items.headline: Used LTO-5 drives bring tape back to homelabs
items.summary: Hackaday covered a homelab builder backing up to a second-hand LTO-5 drive, noting that used tapes cost far less per terabyte than the cheapest new hard drives. Used drives need care: see our buying advice for used drives.

items.headline: TapeArk moves old tape archives into cloud virtual tape libraries
items.summary: TapeArk reads customers' legacy tapes at its own ingest centres and loads the data into virtual tape libraries in public cloud, accessed through its Nexus platform.

items.headline: Still no half-height LTO-10 drive
items.summary: As of mid-October 2026, IBM and Quantum sell LTO-10 drives only as full-height units inside their libraries, and HPE's current drive specifications list LTO-8 and LTO-9 only. Stand-alone buyers are still choosing LTO-9 drives.
items.source: IBM, Quantum and HPE product pages

items.headline: LTO shipments fell 9% in 2025, then rose 57% in the first quarter of 2026
items.summary: The LTO Program reported 160.3 EB shipped in 2025, down from the 176.5 EB record in 2024, and a 57% year-on-year rise in the first quarter of 2026. The LTO Program re-posted the coverage on 10 October.
